newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch stocks were boosted late in the session on Thursday by a firm start on Wall Street, sending the AEX index of blue chips to another record close.
Early negative sentiment was gradually turned around during the day, as the domestic bond market edged higher.

The AEX index closed 3.74 points higher at 685.02 points, beating the previous record close of 681.28 scored on Wednesday. It peaked at an intra-day record just ahead of the close of 686.01, outpacing Wednesday's 685.10 points.
"We saw some profit-taking early but then once again good buying came in, on financials and cyclicals," one dealer said.

Philips, one of the early casualties, was active all day and finished 30 cents ahead at 75.40 guilders. The electronics giant announced it was cutting its stake in chip equipment maker ASM Lithography in a move which could raise some 400 million guilders. Analysts took the view the deal as further evidence of a turnaround at Philips although the company denied the sale was part of its strategy to weed out what chairman Cor Boonstra has called underperforming "bleeders" from the group.
"Although the company is not on the right track yet, we feel that the management has a much clearer picture of what the right track is," an analyst at ING Barings Research said.
ASM Lithography itself posted 1996 net profits of 218 million guilders, up 66 percent on the year before. It also announced plans for a two-for-one stock stock split.

The shares were punished early on, falling more than six percent to a low at 102.00 guilders. Dealers ascribed the fall to profit-taking after a decent run-up recently. But the price gradually improved and finished up 1.00 at 112.00 guilders.

Brokerage Wesselius Securities upgraded the stock to a buy, saying it believed the company had manoevred itself to benefit from an upturn in semi-conductor demand. It also trades to a large discount to international peers, it added.

Elsewhere, financials improved through the day as the prospects for the bond market brightened. Both banking groups ING and ABN AMRO fell early but both managed to claw back losses and finish in positive territory.
ING closed up 0.30 guilders at 75.40, off an early low at 73.30 and ABM AMRO ended just 0.10 up at 121.10 guilders.
